As a Sendae user, I want to create an account with my name, email and password, so I can start a private publishing workspace.

Name is required (100 characters maximum); email is unique and normalized; confirmed password is at least 8 characters and at most 72 bytes on the server. Success returns to sign-in; email verification is not required.
As a Sendae user, I want to sign in using email and password, so I can open my own cached workspace.

Successful authentication stores a service token and account identity, selects the default workspace, and loads local state. Wrong credentials return an error; existing data for other workspaces remains intact.
As a Sendae user, I want to keep workspace content hidden until sign-in, so I can prevent use of my workspace after sign-out.

The signed-out screen hides all workspace pages. Local operations and local MCP require a valid stored session; hosted operations require an authenticated scoped token. Password reset handoffs remain accessible.

As a Sendae user, I want to store my desktop login securely, so I can stay signed in without exposing my token.

Settings use Laravel encryption. In NativePHP, session tokens are additionally sealed with OS encryption; unavailable secure storage fails with an error. Cached draft content itself is not encrypted by this mechanism.
As a Sendae user, I want to sign out of my account, so I can close access to my workspace.

Pending edits are saved first. The service token is revoked before local credentials and visible state are cleared; a remote failure preserves the local session. Cached workspace records are retained for later sign-in.
As a Sendae user, I want to request a reset email, so I can recover access without revealing whether an address is registered.
The response is generic for known and unknown addresses. Production reset requests reject unavailable mail configuration. The emailed reset link opens the desktop reset form.
As a Sendae user, I want to choose a new password from my reset link, so I can regain access and invalidate old sessions.

The token and email must match and the confirmed password must pass validation. Reset tokens are single-use; server access tokens, refresh tokens and sessions are revoked. The desktop returns to sign-in.
As a Sendae user, I want to read and clear sign-in errors, so I can correct invalid input.
Sign-in, registration and recovery errors render as alerts. Switching authentication mode clears errors and passwords; pending requests disable submission.
As a Sendae user, I want to change my account name, so I can keep my identity current.
Settings persist a required name of up to 100 characters through the service and immediately update the displayed identity. A name-only change does not require the current password.
As a Sendae user, I want to change my account email, so I can use my preferred sign-in address.
The server normalizes the address, requires uniqueness and a valid current password when the email changes. Returned identity updates the desktop. No verification-email gate is introduced.
As a Sendae user, I want to set a new password while signed in, so I can update my credentials.

Current password and matching confirmation are required for a new password. The server enforces at least 8 characters and at most 72 bytes. Successful updates clear password fields; this path does not revoke other tokens.
As a Sendae user, I want to see an avatar for my account email, so I can recognize my signed-in identity.
The desktop hashes normalized email with SHA-256 and requests a Gravatar with identicon fallback. It refreshes when the email changes; if browser crypto is unavailable, no Gravatar is requested.
As a Sendae user, I want to receive a personal workspace on registration, so I can start without configuring workspace storage.
A new user receives a default Personal workspace. Data access is scoped to the authenticated owner and selected workspace.

As a Sendae user, I want to create another named workspace, so I can separate publishing contexts under one account.

The sidebar opens a name/image form. A required name up to 100 characters creates an owned workspace; absent icons use the first letter. The desktop saves pending edits before switching to the new workspace.
As a Sendae user, I want to switch between my workspaces, so I can work with the right accounts and drafts.

Switching saves pending editor changes, checks workspace ownership, resets the editor/search/dialogs, and reloads the selected workspace. Other workspaces remain stored locally; requests carry the active workspace ID.
As a Sendae user, I want to rename my workspace, so I can identify its purpose.
Settings opens the existing workspace form. Saving updates the server name and locally cached workspace list. A blank or overlong name is rejected.
As a Sendae user, I want to set a workspace picture, so I can recognize the workspace quickly.
Accept JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 2 MB. Show a local preview, upload to the owned workspace, cache locally, and display the image across workspace controls.
As a Sendae user, I want to remove a workspace picture, so I can return to the workspace initial.
Removal deletes the server and cached image. Workspace avatars fall back to the icon/first letter; a later sync must not restore the deleted image.
As a Sendae user, I want to see workspace pictures while using local state, so I can recognize workspaces between synchronizations.

Signed-in local image requests serve cached files. Sync fetches missing images, removes images no longer present, and skips files already cached. Existing cached images are not redownloaded merely because a remote image changed.
Verify cross-device image replacement; cache lookup currently skips an existing image file.
As a Sendae user, I want to delete an unwanted workspace, so I can remove its content and connections from Sendae.

Confirmation identifies the workspace. Server success removes drafts, publications, accounts and media and chooses an owned remaining workspace; the desktop then removes cached data. Live social posts remain unchanged.

Deleting the only workspace is rejected. Publishing or uncertain work blocks deletion until resolved. Other owners cannot delete the workspace and failures retain local state.

As a Sendae user, I want to open Posts, Calendar, Published, Activity, Analytics, Accounts and Settings, so I can manage the publishing workflow.

Sidebar navigation uses one shared workspace instance. The editor and polling survive page changes. Posts and Calendar show their current counts; Calendar includes an Attention subview for unresolved publications.
As a Sendae user, I want to return to the last selected sidebar page after reload, so I can resume my workflow.
Session storage remembers the selected page. Legacy Queue maps to Calendar; unknown or inaccessible saved values fall back to Posts.
As a Sendae user, I want to choose a color theme, so I can use a comfortable interface.
Settings provides Light, Dark and System. The choice persists in local storage; System follows media-query changes and the active theme also configures notifications.

As a Sendae user, I want to use keyboard shortcuts, so I can work quickly without leaving text editing unsafe.

Command/Control-N creates a post; Command-comma opens Settings. Command/Control-A selects visible posts outside editable fields/dialogs/menus; unmodified Backspace confirms deletion. Escape closes scheduling, slots and recovery dialogs.
As a Sendae user, I want to see actionable progress and errors, so I can know whether work completed.

The app shows loading and busy states. Signed-in success/error toasts have close controls and a 5-second duration; authentication and modal errors remain inline. Routine successful sync and autosave stay quiet.
As a Sendae user, I want to use dialogs with keyboard and pointer controls, so I can complete focused actions.
Native dialog elements open modally, have labelled headings, and provide cancel/close behavior. Busy protections vary by dialog; recovery and workspace dialogs refuse dismissal while busy.
As a Sendae user, I want to run Sendae as a desktop app, so I can keep my publishing workspace open.
NativePHP opens a window titled Sendae at 1280 × 850 with a minimum 900 × 640 size. Responsive layouts exist for narrower content regions.
As a Sendae user, I want to identify Sendae in the Dock and installed apps, so I can find the application.
Build preparation compiles Icon Composer assets and patches NativePHP/Electron installation paths so development and packaged apps use the supplied icon.
As a Sendae user, I want to open password-reset, social-connection and assistant-consent handoffs, so I can continue browser or email workflows in the app.

Only valid sendae:// actions and validated token/ticket fields are accepted. A cached handoff expires after 10 minutes, is consumed once, and is polled every 1.5 seconds. Signed-out connection/consent requests wait for sign-in.

As a Sendae user, I want to be notified when a post becomes published, so I can learn about completed publishing.
The first sync establishes a baseline without historical notifications. Later newly published IDs notify once per workspace, only inside NativePHP; publication title comes from its saved snapshot.
As a Sendae user, I want to receive app updates through the configured updater, so I can keep my installed app current.
NativePHP updater configuration exists but is disabled by default. It requires a packaged build and a configured distribution provider; source configuration alone does not establish working delivery.
Verify release distribution and updater configuration in a packaged build before enabling.
As a Sendae user, I want to start a new post, so I can capture an idea immediately.
Create a UUID draft with blank optional title, one empty item, no overrides or accounts, and version 0. Save locally, select it, open Posts, and clear search so it is visible.
As a Sendae user, I want to name a draft or leave its name blank, so I can organize posts without changing published text.

Titles are internal labels up to 200 characters. Unnamed posts display up to 60 characters of opening text or Photo/Video/Media/New post fallback. Legacy timestamp titles display as previews without rewriting stored values.
As a Sendae user, I want to search my unpublished drafts, so I can find content quickly.
Search matches case-insensitive display title and content from shared/network variants. Published drafts are excluded; no-match state offers Clear search.
View draft destination and status summary
As a Sendae user, I want to see draft status and selected networks, so I can understand what will happen to each post.

Rows show updated time, per-status destination counts, network logos, custom-version dots, no-account state and thread count. Empty cancelled publications do not make an otherwise unscheduled draft look queued.
As a Sendae user, I want to switch or close a draft after saving, so I can retain my edits.

Opening a different draft or closing the composer waits for pending saves. Save failure keeps the current draft available; opening the same draft preserves its current content. Published drafts redirect to Published.
As a Sendae user, I want to save edits as I type, so I can avoid a manual save step.

Every change queues a local save. Saves serialize and continue for edits made during an earlier save. Success updates the stored version; failures retain pending content and show an unsaved/error state.
Warn before closing with unsaved edits
As a Sendae user, I want to be warned before unloading unsaved work, so I can avoid losing pending edits.
A beforeunload handler blocks unannounced closing while edits are pending or a save is active. It does not claim unsaved browser memory survives a forced termination.
As a Sendae user, I want to choose one or more social accounts, so I can publish to the intended destinations.
Connected accounts are selectable. Already selected expired accounts remain visible with reconnect guidance and can be removed. Scheduling requires valid connected destinations.
As a Sendae user, I want to write shared content, so I can reuse a message across networks.

Text and attachment IDs are saved as ordered items. The composer does not display live character totals. Network validation messages appear only for destinations with errors; local draft validation still allows empty text while drafting, at most 30 items, and at most 65,000 characters per item.
As a Sendae user, I want to add or remove thread items, so I can publish multi-part content.
Shared, X, Threads and Bluesky versions allow adding items. Removing an item is offered when more than one remains. Publishing submits each item in order using confirmed reply receipts.

As a Sendae user, I want to edit content specifically for a network, so I can adapt a shared draft without changing other networks.

Viewing a network makes a working copy but creates no saved override until edited. The override is keyed by provider, so accounts on the same network share it; text and media survive reopening and later shared edits.
As a Sendae user, I want to return a network to shared content, so I can remove a custom version deliberately.
Use shared draft deletes the selected provider override, returns to the shared tab and autosaves. Shared edits warn when selected networks retain custom versions.
As a Sendae user, I want to reuse thread content on Facebook and LinkedIn, so I can publish a single feed post without dropping content.
Facebook and both LinkedIn destinations combine item text with blank lines and concatenate all media IDs. Their combined content must still pass that network’s length and media limits.
As a Sendae user, I want to select individual posts or ranges, so I can perform bulk actions.
Command/Control-click toggles; Shift-click selects a visible range; combined modifiers add ranges. Select all respects search. Page, authentication and workspace changes clear selection.
As a Sendae user, I want to delete selected posts after confirmation, so I can remove unwanted drafts safely.

Deletion waits for any active autosave, confirms server deletion before local removal, and cancels scheduled/retry destinations. Published posts stay live. Partial batch failure removes confirmed deletions and retains remaining selections.

As a Sendae user, I want to right-click or use Shift-F10 on a post, so I can act on that post or its selection.
Context-menu deletion targets the clicked row unless it is already in a multi-selection. The menu fits the viewport, focuses its action, restores row focus, and dismisses without deleting.
As a Sendae user, I want to retain deleted state across devices, so I can prevent stale sync recreating removed posts.

The server checks the current synced version and rejects publishing/uncertain work. Deleted drafts retain tombstones and stale uploads receive 410. Remote failure or version conflict keeps local data for review.
As a Sendae user, I want to view completed posts as publications, so I can avoid editing already-live content by mistake.

Posts remains visible and editable while any destination is queued, publishing, failed, missed or uncertain, even if another is published. Fully completed drafts leave Posts and local saves return 409. Published destinations are labelled unchanged; schedule updates preserve completed snapshots and receipts. Failed/missed/uncertain destinations offer recovery beside the composer.
Recover failed destinations individually before editing their saved publication. Hosted draft saves can still change the underlying draft; completed publication snapshots stay immutable.

As a Sendae user, I want to edit a scheduled post whose draft was tombstoned, so I can manage existing queued content.

Queued snapshots reconstruct an editable draft representation. Explicit restore is allowed only with scheduled/retry publications and no confirmed receipts; normal stale saves cannot restore a deleted draft.
As a Sendae user, I want to upload media to a draft item, so I can include visual content.
Multiple JPEG/PNG/WebP/MP4/MOV files can be chosen. Each file is validated by MIME and limited to 100 MB; successful media are stored locally and attached by UUID. Failed storage cleans up the file.
Remove an attachment from a post
As a Sendae user, I want to detach selected media, so I can change a post’s attachments.
Remove attachment deletes its ID from that item and autosaves. It does not delete the underlying library file or reclaim server storage.
Underlying media has no individual deletion or automatic cleanup flow.
As a Sendae user, I want to inspect an attached image or play a video, so I can check the content before scheduling.
Images use local media routes and descriptive fallback alt text; videos show native controls. File reads require sign-in and active-workspace binding; responses use private caching and nosniff.
As a Sendae user, I want to upload local media before syncing drafts, so I can make scheduled content available to the server.
Unsynced media upload by stable UUID before dirty drafts. Already known IDs replay their media record. Missing local copies of server media download after state refresh.
As a Sendae user, I want to receive a clear error when storage is full, so I can keep local content while resolving capacity.

The server enforces a configurable workspace attachment quota (default 1 GiB) before writing new media. Repeated UUID uploads do not consume a second record. The desktop has no quota-management interface.
Check quota boundaries; no automatic retention or per-file deletion is implemented.
As a Sendae user, I want to preview the selected account’s content, so I can review network-specific appearance.
A modal lets users choose destination accounts and previews their own shared or overridden content. With no destination, it shows a placeholder account. Previews do not change the draft.
As a Sendae user, I want to see a network-style post preview, so I can check text, identity and attachments.

The six providers have distinct action rows and identity treatment. Threads media scrolls as a carousel; other previews display four media tiles plus overflow count. Long Facebook/LinkedIn text expands with See more. Preview actions are decorative.
As a Sendae user, I want to recognize links and hashtags in previews, so I can read the draft as a social post.

Preview text recognizes HTTP(S), bare domains and hashtags, avoids emails/version-like strings, preserves punctuation and escapes text. X links use shortened display labels; underlying draft text is unchanged.
As a Sendae user, I want to see website metadata for text-only items, so I can check how shared links may appear.

After a 500 ms debounce, the first URL per text-only item fetches metadata. X prefers Twitter metadata; other providers use Open Graph. Media removes cards; stale requests are aborted and failures leave text links.
As a Sendae user, I want to fetch previews without reaching private services, so I can protect the local machine.

Preview requests require sign-in, are throttled and cached for 10 minutes. Fetches permit HTTP(S) on ports 80/443 with public IPv4 resolution pinned, revalidate redirects, and bound HTML/image sizes. IPv6-only hosts are not supported.
As a Sendae user, I want to understand what the preview represents, so I can avoid assuming it exactly matches a live post.

The preview is a visual approximation. Bluesky publishing emits URL facets and image embeds, but no website-card embed; the desktop can nevertheless show a website card. Network-native rendering remains provider-controlled.
Verify live rendering; distinguish desktop cards from provider payload capabilities.
As a Sendae user, I want to see which networks can connect, so I can understand available destinations.

Accounts lists X, Bluesky, Threads, Facebook, LinkedIn profile and LinkedIn Page. Configured and approved providers get Connect; others show Coming soon or Awaiting approval. These are server-supplied capability flags.

As a Sendae user, I want to connect a provider in my browser, so I can authorize Sendae without entering its credentials in the desktop.

The authenticated server issues a one-use connection ticket bound to owner/workspace. The desktop opens only the fixed service’s connection URL; tickets expire after 10 minutes. Browser handoff exchanges provider consent for a desktop selection ticket.
As a Sendae user, I want to select accounts after provider consent, so I can connect only intended profiles or Pages.

The desktop shows eligible account names and a timezone. At least one unique valid selection is required. Selection writes to the workspace where the flow began, even after a workspace switch; tickets are owner-bound and consumed once.

As a Sendae user, I want to authorize my X account, so I can publish tweets and threads.

OAuth uses PKCE and requests tweet read/write, user read, offline access and media write. The returned user identity becomes a connected destination. Provider app credentials and permissions are required.
Live X consent and publishing were not exercised.
As a Sendae user, I want to authorize my Threads account, so I can publish posts and threads.
OAuth requests basic, publishing and insights permissions, attempts a long-lived token exchange, and returns the profile for desktop selection.
Live Threads consent and publishing were not exercised.
As a Sendae user, I want to choose Pages I may publish to, so I can manage business publishing.

OAuth requests Page and business permissions. The adapter lists up to 100 Pages and offers those with CREATE_CONTENT or MANAGE tasks; stored Page access tokens are kept server-side. Personal Facebook timelines are not supported.
No pagination beyond the first 100 returned Pages; live Page permissions need verification.
As a Sendae user, I want to authorize my personal LinkedIn profile, so I can publish profile posts.
Profile OAuth uses its own client credentials and openid/profile/w_member_social scopes. Optional personal analytics scope is requested only when enabled.
Live LinkedIn profile consent and posting were not exercised.
As a Sendae user, I want to authorize organization publishing, so I can publish to eligible Company Pages.

A separate Page app requests organization permissions, without openid/profile. Approved ADMINISTRATOR or CONTENT_ADMIN roles are offered from the first 100 ACL results. Connection is gated by LINKEDIN_PAGES_APPROVED, false by default.
Requires organization access approval and Page app configuration; live approval state was not inspected.
As a Sendae user, I want to use a Bluesky handle and app password, so I can connect without browser OAuth.

The desktop submits handle/app password to the fixed service and clears the password after each attempt. The server uses bsky.social, validates the active session, and stores only encrypted session tokens. Self-hosted PDS selection is absent.
Supports Bluesky-hosted accounts; live sign-in was not exercised.

As a Sendae user, I want to refresh account connection state, so I can see newly connected or expired accounts.
Entering Accounts triggers background sync; Refresh requests a manual sync. After browser connection starts, short polling continues for up to two minutes while Accounts stays open.
As a Sendae user, I want to recognize each connected account, so I can avoid selecting the wrong destination.

As a Sendae user, I want to restore a provider authorization, so I can resume publishing after expiry.
Expired connections stay visible with a reconnect action when the provider is available. New selection updates the existing provider identity, credentials and timezone; posting slots are retained.
As a Sendae user, I want to refresh eligible tokens automatically, so I can continue publishing without repeated login.

X refreshes with its refresh token; Threads refreshes a still-valid near-expiry token; Bluesky refreshes within five minutes of expiry. Unsupported or failed expired authorizations require reconnect. Tokens are not exposed in workspace responses.
As a Sendae user, I want to disconnect after confirmation, so I can stop future publishing to that account.

Disconnect clears credentials and marks the account disconnected, hiding it from the active account list. Scheduled/retry publications are cancelled; in-flight/uncertain/published records remain. Live posts are not deleted.
As a Sendae user, I want to set weekly days, times and account timezone, so I can schedule into a recurring posting calendar.

A per-account dialog adds/removes day/time entries and validates an IANA timezone, day 0–6, HH:mm time and at most 100 slots. Saving changes future slot selection, not existing exact publication times.
As a Sendae user, I want to choose a future date and time, so I can publish when intended.
The desktop converts the local datetime to an ISO instant. The server requires an explicit offset or Z, a current draft version, connected destinations and valid content; past times are rejected.
As a Sendae user, I want to send the latest saved draft immediately, so I can post without choosing a date.

Post now flushes local edits, synchronizes content, and creates due publications with queued per-account jobs after commit. It opens Calendar for a new publication; actual completion depends on the worker.
As a Sendae user, I want to queue a post for each account’s next free slot, so I can use my recurring schedule.

Each destination searches its local weekly slots over up to 370 days, chooses the earliest future unoccupied instant, and errors if no slots or free time exists. Accounts may receive different publication times.
As a Sendae user, I want to schedule against account-local clock time, so I can handle seasonal clock changes predictably.

Weekly times follow the account timezone and store UTC instants. Nonexistent spring-forward slots are skipped; repeated autumn times use Carbon’s first occurrence. Calendar displays actual instants in device-local time.
As a Sendae user, I want to reject invalid content for any selected network, so I can avoid partially scheduling an invalid request.

The composer reports per-account, per-item counts and errors before scheduling: provider text limits, empty content, disconnected accounts, missing attachments, image/video counts, and Bluesky type/2 MB/3,000-byte limits. It respects overrides and flattened Facebook/LinkedIn content. Invalid checks disable publishing; the server remains authoritative and rolls back all destinations on validation failure.
X counts intentionally match the server’s conservative Unicode/URL weighting. Provider availability and public media reachability remain server checks.

Schedule from the latest saved content
As a Sendae user, I want to wait for current edits and synchronization, so I can publish the version I reviewed.
Desktop remote operations compare the submitted snapshot or version, push media/drafts, recheck the content and substitute the synced version. A mismatch fails before remote scheduling.
As a Sendae user, I want to retry a failed schedule request, so I can avoid creating duplicate publications.

The desktop persists a request UUID by workspace and payload until success. The server persists operation receipts. Retrying the same request returns its original result; a new confirmed action gets a new identity.
As a Sendae user, I want to reject another pending schedule for the same draft, so I can avoid accidentally double-queuing work.

New scheduling rejects existing scheduled, retry, publishing or uncertain work. A mix of published and failed/missed destinations must be recovered individually to prevent resending completed copies. Explicit update alters active schedules; cancelled publications do not block a new identified action.
As a Sendae user, I want to retain the content chosen when scheduling, so I can separate publishing records from draft changes.
Each destination stores title/items in its own snapshot. Saving a draft alone does not overwrite that snapshot. Desktop edits to active schedules explicitly submit an update after autosave.
As a Sendae user, I want to edit scheduled content directly, so I can update queued posts without a separate save action.

Autosave sends preserve/update scheduling. Queued destinations retain times; removed queued destinations cancel; new ones inherit the earliest queued time. Published, failed and missed destinations are left unchanged. Publishing, uncertain and receipt-bearing active records reject updates; recover unfinished records separately.
As a Sendae user, I want to retry a queued-content update after saving locally, so I can keep edits while resolving publication problems.
The draft remains saved when the schedule update fails. The composer reports that queued content was not updated and offers Manage accounts and Retry update; editing and navigation remain available.
As a Sendae user, I want to choose a new time or mode for a scheduled draft, so I can move all remaining destinations together.
Change date & time uses explicit update mode, retaining publication identities where possible. Exact/now/queue modes reset retry timing and errors; invalid or started work rejects the whole update.
As a Sendae user, I want to remove a draft from the queue, so I can return it to editable draft status.

The schedule dialog cancels all currently scheduled/retry destinations after saving edits and retains content/receipts. If a race changes status, completed cancellations are refreshed and remaining work stays visible.
As a Sendae user, I want to view queued publications by day, so I can plan my publishing schedule.

A Monday-first month grid includes surrounding days, queued scheduled/retry/publishing records, device timezone, Today, and previous/next month controls. Selecting a day filters its agenda; Show all removes the filter.
As a Sendae user, I want to switch the calendar to a list, so I can review every queued destination chronologically.
The list includes all queued publications sorted by scheduled time and exposes applicable reschedule/unschedule controls. Empty queue/day states provide clear feedback.
Group destinations at the same time
As a Sendae user, I want to see one heading for a multi-account post, so I can avoid duplicate-looking calendar entries.
Calendar and queue list group by draft ID plus scheduled instant. Account-specific controls remain available; different times and independent drafts remain separate.
As a Sendae user, I want to change an individual publication’s date and time, so I can move one account independently.

Only scheduled/retry records accept a new future valid local datetime. If its draft still has other destinations, the server creates a separate draft from that publication’s snapshot and removes that account from the original. The recovery dialog explains when one destination becomes a separate post; a success notice identifies the split and says other destinations retain their schedules. Before splitting a destination, local changes synchronize; after recovery the editor reloads the remaining account list.
